InnoPharm Biotech - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the InnoPharm Biotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss InnoPharm Biotech's financial results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO of InnoPharm Biotech.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. InnoPharm Biotech delivered a strong performance in the Q3, driven by major regulatory milestones, robust growth across our key franchises, resilient pricing dynamics, and disciplined execution on our strategic priorities. We continue to advance our precision medicine platform and innovative pipeline, positioning us for sustained leadership in oncology, rare diseases, and beyond.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives. We've made transformative progress on regulatory approvals and label expansions, including full FDA approval for INN-301 in frontline NSCLC and EMA expansion for INN-142 into younger pediatric patients, unlocking substantial commercial potential. Our product franchises showed impressive volume and pricing resilience, with oncology leading the way. We've also navigated a complex pricing and reimbursement environment effectively while embedding conservative key assumptions into our outlook. We are particularly excited about INN-301 and its potential to capture significant share in the frontline NSCLC market through our proprietary biomarker and competitive positioning.

Now, I will turn the call over to Michael Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Chen, CFO:
Thank you, Dr. Rivera, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to dive into one of the most transformative quarters for InnoPharm Biotech in our history, particularly on the regulatory front. As Dr. Rivera highlighted, in Q3, we achieved three major milestones: full FDA approval for our lead oncology asset, INN-301, in frontline metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, or NSCLC; EMA label expansion for our rare disease flagship, INN-142, into pediatric patients under 12 years; and PMDA approval in Japan for INN-301 as a second-line therapy. These wins not only validate our precision medicine platform but also unlock over $2.5 billion in combined peak sales potential across global markets, with a projected 25-30% revenue uplift to our 2025 guidance of $1.8-2.0 billion.

Let me break this down achievement by achievement, including the clinical and commercial implications.

First, the FDA's full approval of INN-301, our next-generation PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy for frontline EGFR-wildtype NSCLC. This builds on our Breakthrough Therapy Designation from Q4 last year and the positive Phase 3 readout from the INNOVATE-3 trial, demonstrating a statistically significant 42% reduction in risk of progression or death—median progression-free survival of 14.8 months versus 9.2 months for standard-of-care pembrolizumab plus chemo, with a hazard ratio of 0.58 and p-value less than 0.0001. Overall survival data are immature but trending favorably with a 28% risk reduction. Importantly, this approval incorporates our proprietary tumor microenvironment biomarker, TVM-Score™, which enriches for responders, delivering a 65% objective response rate in TVM-high patients compared to 38% in the overall intent-to-treat population.

Commercially, this positions INN-301 to enter a $15 billion addressable frontline NSCLC market, currently led by products like Keytruda and Tecentriq. We anticipate $850 million in U.S. peak sales by 2028, with a Q4 launch ramping to $120 million in initial-year uptake, supported by 45% gross-to-net adjustments and a competitive wholesale acquisition cost of $168,000 per patient-year—about 10% below the category average. We've obtained J-code assignment and coverage on 85% of Medicare Part D formularies at Tier 3 with minimal restrictions, setting us up for rapid market share gains from Roche and Merck.

On the global front, this U.S. approval supports our marketing authorization application filing with the EMA in Q1 2025, using cross-acceptance of INNOVATE-3 data, and we've started rolling submissions to China's NMPA under their expedited oncology pathway. In Japan, the PMDA approval for second-line use—based on bridging data from INNOVATE-2—represents our first approval in Asia, accessing a $1.2 billion market with 90% reimbursement under the yakka system. Early access programs have already generated $15 million in named-patient sales this quarter.

Moving to INN-142, our gene-corrected autologous CAR-T therapy for relapsed/refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia in pediatric patients. The EMA's label expansion from adolescents to those under 12, fulfilling our Paediatric Investigation Plan, is transformative for this ultra-rare indication. Data from the EXPAND-1 extension cohort showed a 78% complete remission rate and 62% minimal residual disease negativity at Day 28 in this younger cohort, with 12-month event-free survival of 52%—doubling historical benchmarks from therapies like blinatumomab or inotuzumab. As an Orphan Drug Designation holder, it now reaches the full $3 billion global pediatric ALL market.

In the EU, we're pricing at €450,000 per treatment, in line with precedents like Kymriah and Yescarta, and have secured HTA reimbursement in Germany with an IQWiG major benefit rating and in France with HAS important SMR. Our supplemental BLA for U.S. label expansion is on track for Q2 2025 approval, with CMS discussions for a pediatric-specific Medicare carve-out underway. This also derisks our manufacturing scale-up at the Ghent facility, now at 150 lots per year after Tech Transfer 2.0, lowering cost of goods sold to 25% of sales.

These approvals reflect our label lifecycle maximization strategy, using real-world evidence from our global PRIME registry with over 2,500 patients to fuel follow-ons like INN-301's adjuvant filing in H2 2026. In a tougher FDA environment following 2023's scrutiny on accelerated approvals—with conversion rates down to 38%—our 100% full-approval rate from BTD assets showcases the strength of our AI-driven patient selection and adaptive trial designs.

Ahead, we have six catalysts in the next 12 months: three label expansions for INN-301 into squamous NSCLC, INN-142 into adult ALL, and INN-089 subcutaneous; two new approvals for INN-089 in obesity via GLP-1/GIP dual agonism in the U.S. and EU; and a PMDA filing for INN-142. Partnerships like Samsung Biologics for Asia capacity and our $300 million CRV from Jefferies affirm this momentum, lifting our pipeline net present value to $12 billion. These successes expand our total addressable market by 40% and strengthen our competitive moat amid biotech consolidation.

With that regulatory context, let's turn to our Q3 financial results. Product revenue totaled $5.2 billion for the quarter, up 14% year-over-year on a reported basis and 16% on a constant-currency basis. This growth highlights the strength of our portfolio despite macroeconomic pressures, payer scrutiny, and biosimilar competition in mature areas.

I'll break it down by our four key franchises—Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, and Cardiovascular—with details on volumes, pricing, prescriptions, and regional trends. All figures are net of discounts, rebates, and chargebacks, with U.S. revenue at 68%, ex-U.S. at 28%, and Emerging Markets at 4%.

Oncology led with $2.35 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 45% of total product revenue. OncoTarget-300, our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific antibody, drove $2.1 billion, up 20%. Volumes increased 12%, with global total prescriptions at 285,000—up 10%—powered by 15% new prescription growth in NSCLC and frontline triple-negative breast cancer post-FDA label expansion. Patient days on therapy rose 8% to 1.2 million, with 12-month persistence at 78%, up from 74%, due to our subcutaneous formulation reducing administration time by 50%.

Average selling price climbed 6% to $145,000 per patient-year, aided by a 4% U.S. WAC increase within IRA limits and favorable combo mix. U.S. revenue hit $1.6 billion, up 22%, with 32% Medicare Part D penetration and stable 42% managed care rebates. Ex-U.S., $650 million grew 14%, boosted by Germany and Japan reimbursements, though France's ASMR clawback tempered ASP growth to 9% constant-currency. Tailwinds include Phase III adjuvant melanoma data in Q4 and 25% yield gains from Singapore manufacturing. We hold 28% global PD-1 market share per IQVIA.

Immunology generated $1.56 billion, up 8% and 30% of total. ImmunoShield, our IL-23 inhibitor, contributed $1.4 billion, up 9%. Volumes were flat at 420,000 total prescriptions, with 5% new Rx growth in psoriasis offset by 22% decline in legacy BioTNF-Alpha to 150,000 Rx. Persistence held at 72% at 24 months via digital apps.

ASP rose 8% to $38,500 per patient-year from U.S. channel shifts and 3% list hikes. U.S. revenue of $1.1 billion grew 10%, with $4,200 rebate per unit flat despite 340B. Ex-U.S., $460 million up 4% constant-currency, strong in China offsetting EU HTA. Our switch program captured 18% of BioTNF scripts, saving $120 million.

Rare Diseases hit $850 million, up 22% and 16% of total, led by GeneFix AAV gene therapy for SMA at $720 million, up 25%. Volumes surged 18% with 2,800 new treatments, driven by U.S. infant screening in 15 states. Durability shows 92% event-free survival at 4 years. ASP up 3% to $2.4 million. U.S. $620 million up 28%, gross-to-net 18%. Ex-U.S. $230 million up 16%. Plasmid-free manufacturing cut COGS 30%, with Duchenne expansion eyed.

Cardiovascular rounded out at $440 million, up 5%, from CardioVast PCSK9 siRNA. Volumes up 7% to 180,000 Rx, persistence 80%. ASP up 2% to $12,800. U.S. $300 million up 6%, ex-U.S. $140 million up 3%.

Overall, volumes drove 9% of growth, price/mix 5%. Ex-U.S. grew 11% constant-currency, Emerging Markets volumes +30%. We're investing $1.2 billion in CapEx for manufacturing and 12 Phase III assets. Q4 guide: $5.4-5.6 billion product revenue, Oncology +17-19% YoY.

As we consider the broader picture, the pricing and reimbursement landscape remains dynamic but navigable through our strategies and diversified high-value assets. In the U.S., 62% of revenue, IRA pressures capped WAC hikes for NovaCure, our PD-1 inhibitor with $1.2 billion trailing sales, at 6.8%—below industry 9.2% per SSR Health—costing 120 basis points in realized price. Gross-to-net for NovaCure is 48%, up from 44%, with 32% PBM rebates and 28% 340B. Yet ASP held at $142,000 per patient-year via RWE on PFS superiority. For GeneX SMA gene therapy at $2.1 million, Part B ASP +6% covers 85% of Medicare, with outcomes-based deals limiting net erosion to 2% YoY.

In Europe, 22% of revenue, EU HTAR brings HTA changes. Germany's IQWiG cut NovaCure 17% initially, mitigated to 12% via discounts. UK NICE CDF preserves £1.8 million for GeneX with 8% clawback cap. France/Italy at 92%/88% of list. Emerging markets grew prices 11% YoY.

Biosimilars accelerate—Humira at 45% U.S. share—but next-gen bispecifics target $180,000 WAC with ORR>60%. $50 million in RWE with Flatiron/Optum unlocks exemptions. Our Pricing Excellence CoE uses AI for 18% better rebate forecasts and companion diagnostics reimbursed at $3,500. FY24 U.S. gross-to-net 46-49%, ex-U.S. flat to +2%; IRA Part D favors biologics. Orphan launches provide $1.5M+ pricing.

Sector pricing growth slowed to 4.1%, but we expect mid-single-digit expansion in H2 for 12-15% revenue growth.

Before closing on financials, let me address our key assumptions and risk factors underpinning guidance, subject to safe harbor. Our FY2024 revenue guide of $4.2 to $4.5 billion assumes 18-22% growth from NovaGLP-7 GLP-1 ramp-up post-Q4 2023 U.S. launch, with $12,500 net pricing after 15% gross-to-net, 65% 12-month persistence via auto-injector. Ex-U.S. $450 million, Europe €10,200 ASP, China 20% penetration post-CFDA Q3. Pipeline: NovaCAR-T19 Ph3 topline Q4 2024 at 75% ORR/50% CR for $3.2B peak; NovaBispec-2 NSCLC Ph3 mid-2025 +25% PFS for $1.8B. R&D: 20% lower Ph2 failure via NovaAI-Discover, OpEx +12%, margins 82%. Macro: IRA 8% impact, $120B biotech funding.

Risks: Ph3 attrition 30%, delaying NovaCAR-T19 NPV $800M; EMA delays; GLP-1 biosimilars 40% ASP erosion; PBM rebates to 25%; IP for NovaSit-4 expiry 2027; manufacturing single-site; forex; rates on $1.2B debt. Mitigants: $200M Resilience Fund, AI pricing, orphan expansions. Base 85% hit probability; misses drop EPS to $2.10 from $3.45.

Our GAAP net income was $420 million, or $2.05 per share. Non-GAAP net income $510 million, or $2.50 per share. Operating expenses $2.1 billion, up 10% reflecting R&D investments in our pipeline—$1.1 billion in R&D alone. Cash position strong at $3.2 billion.

For full year, we're raising guidance to $20.5-21.0 billion in revenue, with adjusted EPS $9.50-$10.00.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Dr. Rivera.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Michael. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, good morning. Congrats on the strong quarter. On the INN-301 launch, can you elaborate on the early access traction in Asia and how TVM-Score differentiates in a crowded NSCLC space?

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thanks, David. Great question. The PMDA second-line approval has been a catalyst, with $15 million in named-patient sales this quarter signaling demand. TVM-Score's 65% ORR in high-expressers gives us a clear edge over Keytruda combos, and our J-code plus formulary wins position us for 10-15% share in year one. Dr. Vasquez can add on the biomarker.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:
Absolutely. The INNOVATE-3 PFS benefit and biomarker enrichment de-risk adoption, with registry data already showing real-world alignment.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen, Morgan Stanley:
Good morning. With IRA and HTA pressures, how confident are you in the pricing assumptions for NovaGLP-7 and oncology assets? Any update on outcomes-based deals?

Michael Chen, CFO:
Hi Lisa. Confidence is high given our RWE and CoE analytics—92% rebate forecast accuracy. For NovaGLP-7, 15% gross-to-net holds with 65% persistence beating peers. Oncology ASPs stable via superior data; GeneX outcomes deals cover 15% volume, limiting erosion. EU HTA mitigated to low-single digits. Upside from orphans.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel, JPMorgan:
Thanks. On risks, how are you addressing CAR-T manufacturing scale for INN-142 expansion and potential Ph3 delays for NovaCAR-T19?

Michael Chen, CFO:
Raj, solid point. Ghent at 150 lots/year post-Tech Transfer 2.0 cuts COGS to 25%; Resilience Fund covers backups. For NovaCAR-T19, lipid nanoparticles keep CRS under 10%, interim Ph2 supports 75% ORR. 30% attrition baked in, but AI de-risking lowers Ph2 failures to 45%.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
To add, our PRIME registry and partnerships like Samsung ensure supply chain resilience.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the InnoPharm Biotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
